quote: Inthepreviouswork[17], sevenMTDtechniqueswereimplemented. claim: The random and alternative deployment strategies follow a schedule, so they are proactive
quote: MTDSimTime utilises time-based proactive MTD execution schemes with various execution strategies. Since these MTD techniques are triggered periodically and do not have reactive concerns, they are all implemented as time-based proactive schemes.

claim: The single deployment strategy follows a schedule, so it is proactive
quote: three specific MTD execution schemes are introduced in this work: random execution, alternative execution, and simultaneous execution.
issue: Zhang's proactive schemes are random, alternative and simultaneous; 'single' is not one of his schemes, only his single-MTD evaluation (Sec. 5.1), which runs on the same periodic trigger but is not called proactive.

claim: Three of the four deployment strategies (random, alternative, single) come from Zhang
quote: three specific MTD execution schemes are introduced in this work: random execution, alternative execution, and simultaneous execution. ... The random execution scheme was used in previous work [17].
locator: Sec. 4.3.2, p. 23 printed (PDF p. 24); Sec. 4.3.2.1, p. 24 printed (PDF p. 25)
issue: Zhang's three named schemes are random, alternative and simultaneous, not single; and he says random 'was used in previous work [17]'. Zhang ran all three of the table's strategies (single as his single-MTD evaluation), but introduced only alternative among them.

claim: A run ends when the attacker compromises more than 80 % of the hosts
quote: we set the terminating condition for the simulation as the NCR reaching 0.8 and run the simulation 100 times for each variable set
issue: Zhang ends a run when NCR 'reaching 0.8' (at least 80 %), in his one (general) scenario; 'more than 80 %' drifts the threshold, and Table 2.4 (U0136) itself says '80 % of the hosts compromised'.
fix_text: "more than 80\,\% of the hosts" -> "80\,\% of the hosts" (unless the code tests strictly greater, in which case cite the code for 'more than')

claim: An exploit of a vulnerability exploited before takes half the time
quote: In terms of the learning capabilities, the attack model is designed to halve the exploitation time spent on the vulnerabilities that were exploited in the previous attack operations conducted on previous hosts.
issue: Adversarial read: Zhang halves exploitation time for vulnerabilities exploited 'in the previous attack operations conducted on previous hosts' (Eq. 2 divides (1-ACv) by 2) -- matches 'exploited before'.

claim: Each disruption costs the attacker a confusion penalty
quote: The adversary in the simulator is designed to take a time penalty to simulate the confusion caused by MTD. The time penalty is assigned each time the attack event is interrupted or stopped by MTD.

claim: The confusion penalty is about 20 s
quote: The adversary in the simulator is designed to take a time penalty to simulate the confusion caused by MTD. The time penalty is assigned each time the attack event is interrupted or stopped by MTD.
issue: Zhang gives no value for the penalty anywhere in the text; the tex comment traces 20 s to constants.py:147, i.e. the released code.

claim: A deployment never takes back a compromised host
quote: It is assumed that the compromised hosts will always stay compromised and can be recognised by the adversary immediately upon regaining access, regardless of any network changes made by MTD techniques.
issue: Zhang states it as an assumption of his model ('It is assumed'); the sentence states it as a fact of the simulator, which is fair for a model description.

claim: A deployment never takes back a stolen credential
quote: After compromising a host, the adversary gains access to all of its users, which they use to launch credential-stuffing attacks on other hosts in the network.
issue: Zhang says the attacker gains a compromised host's users for credential stuffing, but says nothing about whether MTD revokes them; his model has no user shuffle. The credential half is not in Zhang (likely true of the code).
fix_text: "or a stolen credential \citep{zhang2023}" -> "or a stolen credential \citep{zhang2023, tay2024code}", or move \citep{zhang2023} to after "a compromised host"

claim: NCR is a defender-side effectiveness metric that measures the network's security
quote: we use Network Compromise Ratio (NCR) as the simulation checkpoint to evaluate MTD techniques and their combinations. ... It helps us measure the effectiveness of our MTD techniques by measuring the time it takes for the adversary to compromise a certain proportion of hosts in the network.
issue: Zhang defines NCR but uses it as 'the simulation checkpoint' for MTTC, not as an outcome metric, and never calls it defender-side; the classification is the dissertation's (Cho's frame).

claim: MTTC is an attacker-side effectiveness metric used by Zhang
quote: Inthisstudy, MTTCisselected as the primary evaluation metric in the simulator
issue: Zhang also notes that from the defender's side MTTC 'can also be interpreted as' MTTF; attacker-side placement still fair.

claim: NCR is a defender-side effectiveness metric (Zhang)
quote: we use Network Compromise Ratio (NCR) as the simulation checkpoint to evaluate MTD techniques and their combinations.
issue: As U0207: in Zhang NCR is a termination checkpoint for MTTC, not a reported metric, and has no attacker/defender side.
